Tanker hit 14 nm NE of Lima (3 Nov)
UKMTO: two unknown projectiles struck a tanker's engine room about 14 nm north-east of Lima, Oman at 19:00 GMT on 3 Nov; no injuries.
2
Only 7 Hormuz crossings (2 Nov)
Windward counted 7 crossings on 2 Nov (1 dark) and 8 on 1 Nov, against 84-140 a day pre-war; a dhow was attacked in the strait on 3 Nov (location approximate).
3
158 ships holding in Gulf (3 Nov), up from 113
straits.live counted 158 AIS-visible ships holding in the Strait and Gulf watch box on 3 Nov; Windward sees 17 empty crude tankers waiting off Fujairah (area approximate).
4
Bypass routes >40% of Gulf exports
Kpler: pipelines avoiding Hormuz carry over 40% of regional exports vs 17% pre-war; Yanbu loadings 2.21 mb/d in 1-25 Oct vs 2.54 in September.
5
Gulf crude 16.1 mb/d in Oct, down ~1 mb/d
Kpler: crude and condensate through Hormuz, Red Sea and Gulf of Oman averaged about 16.1 mb/d in October vs 17.09 in September (89% of pre-war 18.0).
6
US 'defensive' strikes on Qeshm (2 Nov)
The US hit an Iranian anti-aircraft site on Qeshm Island after Iranian fire at a US aircraft; Trump called it a 'minor attack' (exact sites not given).
7
Tanker hit 72 nm E of Ras Al Khafji (1 Nov)
UKMTO: a tanker was hit by two projectiles at 23:47 UTC on 1 Nov, about 72 nm east of Ras Al Khafji; crew safe.
GULF OIL FLOWS · updated 4 Nov 2026

Less oil is moving out of the Gulf than before the war: Kpler counts about 16.1 mb/d of crude and condensate across Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Oman in October, down about 1 mb/d from September, and Vortexa puts Gulf crude at 14.0 mb/d, about 86% of pre-war. Hormuz itself is still mostly blocked by attacks: Windward saw only 7-8 crossings a day on 1-2 Nov, and a tanker was hit 14 nm north-east of Lima, Oman on 3 Nov, so bypass routes via Yanbu and Fujairah carry over 40% of exports. Talks stalled this week after Iran called the US reply to its Hormuz plan 'not convincing', and AIS-visible ships holding in the Gulf rose to 158 on 3 Nov from 113.
